recipe: Raw new/delete is a smell: R.11 avoid them, R.20 unique_ptr for exclusive ownership, R.21 prefer unique_ptr over shared_ptr unless sharing, R.23 make_unique. A T* is non-owning (R.3).

C++17 housekeeping: auto_ptr removed, random_shuffle removed, dynamic exception specifications removed, register removed, std::iterator deprecated. Mark result-carrying functions [[nodiscard]]; reason string and constructor/type forms are C++20.

Unscoped enum leaks enumerators into the enclosing scope and converts implicitly to int; enum class does neither — static_cast out, or std::to_underlying (C++23). Fix the underlying type only when size/ABI demands.

C++11 mechanical wins still missing from older code: typedef to using (plus alias templates), NULL/0 to nullptr, override and final on overrides, throw() to noexcept, defaulted/deleted functions instead of private-undefined tricks.
replaces: typedef, NULL, unmarked overrides, private-undefined copy ctors

recipe: enable_if/SFINAE to concepts and requires-clauses: constraints are compile-time predicates checked early in instantiation, so diagnostics name the unsatisfied concept instead of fifty lines of substitution noise; subsumption orders overloads.

Iterator pairs to ranges algorithms and views: lazy, composable with |, less error-prone. borrowed_range and ranges::dangling stop you returning iterators into temporaries. ranges::to plus zip/enumerate/chunk/stride views arrive in C++23.

(pointer, length) parameters to std::span: non-owning contiguous view, static or dynamic extent encoded in the type, satisfies the view concept, TriviallyCopyable since C++23. Stop passing T* plus a size nobody validates.
replaces: T* ptr, size_t n parameter pairs

recipe: const std::string& parameters to std::string_view — no allocation for literals. Caveat cppreference states outright: it is the programmer's responsibility that the character array outlives the view; string_view{"x"s} dangles at the semicolon.

Six hand-written comparison operators to auto operator<=>(const T&) const = default: == is implicitly declared, !=/</>/<=/>= are rewritten candidates. Pick strong_ordering, weak_ordering or partial_ordering deliberately — only partial allows incomparable values.

printf and iostream chains to std::format (C++20), std::print/std::println (C++23). The format string is compile-time checked through std::format_string — an invalid one is a compilation error. Runtime format strings go through std::vformat.

std::thread to std::jthread: the destructor requests stop and joins, so a still-joinable thread no longer calls std::terminate. Take std::stop_token as the first parameter and poll stop_requested() for cooperative cancellation.
replaces: std::thread plus manual join/detach and ad-hoc atomic<bool> flags

recipe: Type punning via reinterpret_cast or unions to std::bit_cast<To>(from) in <bit>: requires equal sizeof and TriviallyCopyable, is constexpr, and dodges the aliasing rule that makes reinterpreting object representation through reinterpret_cast undefined.

Modules contested: real build-hygiene gains, but cppreference records only partial support — GCC 11, Clang 8, MSVC partial; import std (C++23) partial in libstdc++ 15 and libc++ 17. Header-heavy codebases still wait.

Error codes plus out-params to std::expected<T,E>: never valueless, chains through and_then/transform/or_else/transform_error, value() throws bad_expected_access. optional (C++17) means absence; expected means failure with a reason.

E-section discipline: throw when a function cannot perform its assigned task, never as control flow; purpose-designed exception types, not built-ins; throw by value, catch by reference; destructors, swap and deallocation never fail; RAII over try/catch.
replaces: catch(...) everywhere, throwing ints/strings, manual cleanup

recipe: Contested: exceptions vs codes. The isocpp FAQ argues codes force error-propagation clutter through dozens of intermediate functions; the same FAQ concedes hard-real-time and safety-critical work (JSF++) cannot guarantee response times with current tooling. Decide per domain.

Make illegal states unrepresentable: P.4 a program should ideally be statically type safe, P.5 prefer compile-time to run-time checking, I.4 interfaces precisely and strongly typed — types are checked documentation. ES.20 always initialize, ES.23 prefer {}.

ES.48 avoid casts; ES.49 if you must cast, use a named cast; ES.50 never cast away const. Named casts are greppable and far less vulnerable to unintended effects than a C-style cast that silently becomes reinterpret_cast.

GSL vocabulary where the language still lacks it: gsl::not_null restricts a pointer to non-null values, gsl::owner marks an owning raw pointer, Expects/Ensures terminate on contract failure, finally for cleanup, narrow as checked narrow_cast.
replaces: unchecked raw pointers, implicit narrowing conversions

recipe: I.11 never transfer ownership through a raw T* or T&; I.13 do not pass an array as a single pointer — (pointer,size) interfaces are error-prone; I.12 declare must-not-be-null pointers not_null; F.21 return a struct instead of out-params.
replaces: owning raw pointer returns, out-parameters, array-as-pointer

recipe: F.7 take T* or T& for general use; smart pointers in signatures only to express lifetime semantics (R.30): unique_ptr<W> by value takes ownership, shared_ptr<W>& may reseat. F.43 never return a pointer or reference to a local.
replaces: const shared_ptr<T>& parameters on functions that only read

recipe: C.20 if you can avoid defining default operations, do; C.21 define or =delete copy, move and destructor as a complete set. C.35 base destructor public+virtual or protected+non-virtual. C.128 exactly one of virtual/override/final. F.6 noexcept when it cannot throw.
replaces: partial rule-of-three, public non-virtual base destructors
source_name: C++ Core Guidelines (C.20, C.21, C.35, C.128, F.6)

recipe: GCC enables -Wnon-virtual-dtor only under -Weffc++, not -Wall/-Wextra — turn it on explicitly, with -Woverloaded-virtual (hidden base virtuals), -Wsuggest-override, -Wold-style-cast, -Wctor-dtor-privacy. These are the C++-specific ones -Wall never gave you.

ASan and TSan cannot be combined — GCC states -fsanitize=thread cannot be combined with -fsanitize=address or -fsanitize=leak. So: one CI job ASan+LSan+UBSan, a separate job TSan. Add -fno-omit-frame-pointer for usable stack traces.

Budget sanitizer cost before wiring CI: ASan roughly 2x slowdown and up to 3x stack, TSan 5-15x time and 5-10x memory, and TSan needs everything compiled with -fsanitize=thread or it misses races and reports false positives.
replaces: assuming sanitizers are cheap enough for every job

recipe: Ship with library hardening on: _LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE=_LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE_FAST is constant-time security-critical checks intended for production; EXTENSIVE after benchmarking; DEBUG never in production. libstdc++'s counterpart is -D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS (bounds and null-smart-pointer checks).

clang-tidy in CI with a checked-in .clang-tidy: cppcoreguidelines-owning-memory, -special-member-functions, -pro-type-reinterpret-cast, bugprone-use-after-move, -dangling-handle, -unchecked-optional-access, modernize-use-nullptr/-override/-using. -warnings-as-errors promotes them; -fix applies mechanical ones.
replaces: compiler warnings as the only static analysis

recipe: Contested: -Werror. Warnings-as-errors across a multi-compiler CI matrix catches rot; baked into the build it breaks downstream users on newer toolchains — code that compiled warning-free with GCC 4.9 will not with GCC 12. Gate it behind a flag.
source_name: Embedded Artistry: -Werror is Not Your Friend

recipe: GoogleTest: ASSERT_* raises a fatal failure and aborts the current function, EXPECT_* is nonfatal — default to EXPECT so one run reports every failure; each test gets a fresh fixture instance. Catch2 v3 is a compiled library, not header-only.
replaces: ASSERT_* everywhere, shared mutable test state

recipe: Example-based tests miss the interesting inputs. RapidCheck (QuickCheck-inspired) generates them: state the invariant, rc::check explores, and a failure is shrunk to a minimal counterexample. Integrates with Google Test, Google Mock and Boost.Test.

Fuzz every parser and deserializer: extern "C" int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t* Data, size_t Size), build with -fsanitize=fuzzer combined with address and/or undefined, keep a seed corpus. libFuzzer is in-process and coverage-guided.
replaces: unit tests alone on untrusted-input code paths

recipe: Never try!: deprecated 1.39, and try is a 2018 reserved word needing r#try. Use ?, which applies From to the error. API guidelines: examples use ?, not try!, not unwrap.

Edition 2018 removed extern crate; dependency names are in scope everywhere. Paths start with crate::, self::, super::, or a crate name; leading :: means external only. foo.rs beside foo/ replaces foo/mod.rs.

mem::uninitialized/mem::zeroed are instant UB for bool, references, enums. Use MaybeUninit (1.36): initialize fully, then assume_init. MaybeUninit::uninit().assume_init() is equally UB — integers included.

Retire lazy_static/once_cell: OnceLock (1.70) for write-once statics, LazyLock (1.80) for lazily initialized ones. OnceLock is never poisoned; a LazyLock initializer that panics poisons unrecoverably — every later access panics.
let-else (1.65): refutable pattern plus diverging else, with bindings landing in the enclosing scope. Replaces match pyramids and if-let rebinding for guard-clause early returns.

async fn and RPIT in traits are stable since 1.75, but such traits are not dyn-compatible and cannot state Send bounds. Keep async-trait for dyn; publish Send/non-Send variants via #[trait_variant::make].
source_name: Rust Blog: async fn and RPIT in traits

recipe: &raw const x / &raw mut x (1.82) replace ptr::addr_of!/addr_of_mut!. Native place-expression syntax: the sound way to point at packed, unaligned or uninitialized fields without ever forming a reference.
Capture identifiers inline in format strings since 1.58: println!("hello {person}"), including in width and precision ({score:width$.precision$}). Trailing positional arguments are legacy noise.
Let chains (if let Some(x) = a && x > 2) stabilized 1.88, edition 2024 only — they depend on that edition's if-let temporary scope change for correct drop order.

Edition 2021 closures capture individual fields, not whole variables. Audit for changed Drop order and lost auto-traits — capturing a raw-pointer field loses the wrapper's Send. cargo fix --edition inserts let _ = &x;.
source_name: Rust Edition Guide: Disjoint capture in closures

recipe: Edition 2021: array.into_iter() yields values (by-value IntoIterator landed 1.53, with a method-call hack for 2015/2018); panic! always formats, so panic!("{}") errors and non-string payloads need panic_any.
source_name: Rust Edition Guide: IntoIterator for arrays; panic macro consistency

recipe: Edition 2024: RPIT captures every in-scope lifetime by default. Narrow it with precise capturing + use<'a, T> (stable 1.82, all editions). The Captures trick and outlives trick are obsolete.
source_name: Rust Edition Guide: RPIT lifetime capture

recipe: Edition 2024 warns unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn: unsafe fn no longer grants its body unsafe powers. Wrap each operation in its own unsafe {} so the obligation is visible per-operation, not per-function.
replaces: implicit unsafe body in unsafe fn

recipe: Edition 2024 denies static_mut_refs: &STATIC_MUT is instantaneous UB even if unused. Prefer atomics, then Mutex/RwLock, then LazyLock/OnceLock; use &raw mut only for FFI with external synchronization.
source_name: Rust Edition Guide: static mut references

recipe: Edition 2024 drops tail-expression temporaries before locals, so returning c.borrow().len() finally compiles. Conversely, code relying on the old extended scope breaks; tail_expr_drop_order flags affected Drop types.
source_name: Rust Edition Guide: Tail expression temporary scope

recipe: Error types implement std::error::Error (only Debug + Display required) and should be Send + Sync + 'static for thread::spawn and downcast_ref. Display: lowercase, concise, no trailing punctuation. Never Result<_, ()>.
Render a wrapped error in source() or in Display, never both, or chains print duplicated. description() deprecated 1.42 and cause() 1.33 — use source(), which supports downcasting.

Libraries: thiserror derives Error/Display without entering your public API — #[from] implies #[source], a field named source is auto-detected, #[error(transparent)] forwards both. Applications: anyhow with context(), bail!, ensure!.

Contested: anyhow::Error in library APIs. It erases the type so callers cannot match failure modes, against C-GOOD-ERR's meaningful error types; defenders cite leaf crates and binaries. Safe default: thiserror at public boundaries.

Mark public enums/structs #[non_exhaustive] from day one: downstream needs _ arms and .. patterns and cannot use struct literals. Adding variants later then stays minor; adding the attribute later is major.
Newtypes give static distinctions at zero cost (Miles vs Kilometers). Prefer Widget::new(Small, Round) over Widget::new(true, false): bool/Option parameters hide meaning and cannot be extended later.
Typestate: encode state in the type, transition by consuming self and returning the next type. Invalid sequences fail to compile at zero runtime cost — no initialized flags, no runtime asserts.
source_name: The Embedded Rust Book: Typestate programming

recipe: Seal a public trait behind a private supertrait when downstream impls are unwanted; adding non-defaulted items then stays a minor release. Cargo's SemVer guide names sealing as the mitigation for that otherwise-major change.

Keep struct fields private — a public field pins the representation and forfeits validation and invariants. Hide complex returns behind newtypes. Eagerly implement common traits; the orphan rule blocks downstream. Implement From, never Into.
source_name: Rust API Guidelines: C-STRUCT-PRIVATE, C-NEWTYPE-HIDE, C-COMMON-TRAITS

recipe: Naming encodes cost: as_ free borrow-to-borrow, to_ expensive (often allocating), into_ consumes owned-to-owned. Getters drop the get_ prefix. Iterator types mirror their methods: iter() gives Iter, into_iter() gives IntoIter.
source_name: Rust API Guidelines: C-CONV, C-GETTER, C-ITER-TY

recipe: Clippy defaults: correctness deny; suspicious, style, complexity, perf warn. pedantic, nursery, restriction, cargo are allow-by-default. restriction is a menu to pick from individually, not a group to enable wholesale.

Set lint levels in Cargo.toml [lints.rust]/[lints.clippy] since Cargo 1.74, inheritable via [workspace.lints]; they never apply to dependencies. Contested: #![deny(warnings)] in source opts out of stability — many use RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" in CI instead.

Declare package.rust-version; Cargo errors on older toolchains and cargo add picks compatible versions. Edition 2024 implies resolver = "3" (MSRV-aware fallback); resolver = "2" (1.51) stops build-dep and proc-macro features leaking into normal deps.
source_name: Rust Edition Guide: Cargo rust-version aware resolver

recipe: Supply-chain gates: cargo audit checks Cargo.lock against the RustSec advisory DB; cargo deny check adds licenses, bans/duplicate versions and trusted sources; cargo semver-checks catches API breaks before publish, though it misses generic and lifetime changes.

Run cargo miri test on any crate containing unsafe: it catches out-of-bounds, use-after-free, misalignment, invalid values, data races, leaks and aliasing violations under Stacked/Tree Borrows. It checks executed paths only — passing is not soundness.

For lock-free code, loom::model permutes concurrent executions under the C11 memory model using loom::sync shims behind --cfg loom. Caveats: SeqCst is modeled as AcqRel, and some load-buffering executions are never explored.

Property tests: proptest composes Strategy values so shrinking respects construction constraints, where quickcheck shrinks per-type via Arbitrary and needs newtypes for variants; proptest can be an order of magnitude slower. Add cargo fuzz for parsers.

Delete namespace/module X {} and /// <reference path>; use ES modules. Docs: "we recommended modules over namespaces in modern code". Namespaces pollute globals and make component dependencies hard to identify.
replaces: namespaces, internal modules, triple-slash path references

recipe: Prefer a const object with as const plus typeof O[keyof typeof O] over enum — handbook: it "keeps your codebase aligned with the state of JavaScript". Never publish ambient const enum: incompatible with isolatedModules, inlines stale values. Contested.
Do not use any outside JS migration — the compiler treats it as "please turn off type checking for this thing". Use unknown for values you do not know or accept blindly, then narrow before use.
source_name: TypeScript Handbook: Declaration Files Do's and Don'ts

recipe: satisfies validates an expression against a type "without changing the resulting type of that expression". An annotation widens and loses specificity; an as cast validates nothing. Use it on config/lookup literals.
replaces: as assertions and widening type annotations on object literals

recipe: Add const to a type parameter — function f<const T>(x: T) — "to cause const-like inference to be the default", instead of making every caller write as const at the call site.

Set verbatimModuleSyntax: imports/exports without a type modifier are left alone, anything with type is dropped entirely. It replaces the deprecated importsNotUsedAsValues and preserveValueImports. Mark type-only imports explicitly.

TypeScript 5.0 implements the ECMAScript standard decorators proposal: no --experimentalDecorators, and decorators may sit before or after export. Legacy experimental decorators are a separate non-standard system — migrate, do not mix.

Docs on moduleResolution: node (renamed node10 in 5.0): "It should no longer be used", and "Do not use classic". Pick node16/nodenext for Node, bundler for bundlers (requires module esnext or preserve).

Prefer // @ts-expect-error to // @ts-ignore: it reports when the suppressed error no longer exists, so stale suppressions get deleted. @ts-ignore "will do nothing if the following line is error-free".

Replace try/finally cleanup with using res = open() (Symbol.dispose) and await using (Symbol.asyncDispose); DisposableStack tracks several resources. Needs lib including esnext.disposable plus polyfills for Symbol.dispose and SuppressedError.

Node runs TypeScript directly: stripping is default since 23.6.0/22.18.0, stable in 25.2.0/24.12.0. Use noEmit, module nodenext, erasableSyntaxOnly, verbatimModuleSyntax. No enums, runtime namespaces, parameter properties, import aliases.
replaces: ts-node and custom loaders for running TypeScript

recipe: strict = noImplicitAny, noImplicitThis, alwaysStrict, strictNullChecks, strictFunctionTypes, strictBindCallApply, strictPropertyInitialization, useUnknownInCatchVariables, strictBuiltinIteratorReturn (5.6). Outside it: noUncheckedIndexedAccess (4.1), noImplicitOverride (4.3), noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature (4.2), noImplicitReturns, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch.

noUncheckedIndexedAccess makes index-signature access "potentially undefined"; it is not enabled by --strict. Contested: it catches real out-of-bounds bugs but litters loop-heavy and tuple code with non-null assertions.

exactOptionalPropertyTypes stops age?: number from implicitly admitting undefined, so an absent key differs from an explicit undefined (matching in). Not part of --strict; enable alongside strictNullChecks.

Model variants as a discriminated union on a literal kind, switch on it, and in default assign to a never binding. "no type is assignable to never" — so adding a member without a case becomes a compile error.
replaces: boolean flag soup and non-exhaustive switches

recipe: TypeScript 5.5 infers type predicates when a function "does not have an explicit return type or type predicate annotation", so .filter(x => x !== undefined) narrows. Hand-write x is T only where inference fails.
useUnknownInCatchVariables (in the --strict family) types catch (e) as unknown rather than any. Narrow with instanceof Error before reading .message; thrown values are not guaranteed to be Errors.

Rethrow with context, not loss: throw new Error("Connecting to database failed.", { cause: err }). ES2022, widely available since September 2021. cause takes any value, so structured { code, values } payloads are legal.
replaces: swallowing or string-concatenating the original error

recipe: Contested: return expected failures as a discriminated union ({ok:true,value} | {ok:false,error}) so callers must narrow, since throw is untyped in TypeScript. Opposing camp keeps exceptions for exceptional paths and calls Result ceremony.
replaces: throwing for all expected failure modes

recipe: "Don't write overloads that differ by type in only one argument position" — use union types. Collapse overloads differing only in trailing parameters into optional parameters. Sort specific signatures before general ones; the first match wins.
replaces: overload sets that unions or optional parameters would cover
source_name: TypeScript Handbook: Declaration Files Do's and Don'ts

recipe: Handbook generic rules: push type parameters down (<T>(arr: T[]), not <T extends any[]>(arr: T), which infers any); use as few as possible; if a parameter appears once, delete it.
replaces: over-constrained generics and single-use type parameters

recipe: "If your types are generated by your source code, publish the types with your source code." Set types/typings, put @types/* in dependencies, and use /// <reference types="..."> — never relative paths into node_modules.
replaces: shipping untyped packages or relative reference paths

recipe: typescript-eslint tiers: recommended ("almost always a bad practice and/or likely bug"), strict (more opinionated), stylistic, each with a -type-checked variant. Contested: docs suggest strict only where many developers are TypeScript-proficient.

Enable @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises (in recommended-type-checked). It "requires type information to run, which comes with performance tradeoffs" — configure languageOptions.parserOptions. Mark deliberate fire-and-forget via void or allowForKnownSafeCalls.

Gate publishes on @arethetypeswrong/cli: it analyzes node10/node16/bundler resolution and flags Masquerading as CJS/ESM, no types, resolution failed, incorrect default export, missing export = — dual-package hazards tsc never reports.
replaces: assuming tsc emit implies correct published types

recipe: skipLibCheck trades type-system accuracy for build time: two libraries can define the same type inconsistently and you will not be told. Docs scope it to duplicate node_modules types or TypeScript upgrades — a workaround, not a default.
replaces: skipLibCheck: true left on permanently by default

recipe: Test types, not only behaviour: expectTypeOf/assertType in *.test-d.ts, run via --typecheck (which invokes tsc --noEmit). "Vitest doesn't run these files, they are only statically analyzed by the compiler."
replaces: trusting runtime tests to cover type-level contracts

recipe: node:test is Stable as of Node v20.0.0: node --test, built-in mock.fn/mock.method/mock.module/mock.timers, --watch, snapshots stable in v23.4.0. It matches .ts/.mts/.cts files unless --no-strip-types.
replaces: pulling in a test framework for dependency-light packages

recipe: Add fast-check properties inside existing Vitest/Jest/Mocha test blocks: arbitraries are "tailored for detecting common real-world mistakes", failures shrink to minimal counterexamples, and a printed seed makes any failure deterministically reproducible.
replaces: example-only unit tests for pure logic

recipe: Snapshots are code: "should be committed alongside code changes, and reviewed as part of your code review process", and Vitest does not write them in CI. Prefer toMatchInlineSnapshot() over unread .snap files.

Writergate: std.io.GenericReader/GenericWriter/AnyReader/AnyWriter are gone. Use non-generic std.Io.Reader and std.Io.Writer; the buffer lives in the interface, supplied by the caller, not in the implementation.

Stdout needs an explicit buffer now: var buf:[4096]u8=undefined; var fw=std.fs.File.stdout().writer(&buf); const w=&fw.interface; try w.print(...); try w.flush(). Forgetting flush silently drops output.
std.ArrayList is the unmanaged type now; the allocator-carrying version moved to std.array_list.Managed (and ArrayListAligned to AlignedManaged). Pass the allocator to append/deinit on every call.
usingnamespace was removed from the language. Re-export declaration by declaration (pub const x = other.x;) or restructure the module. No namespace injection or mixin idiom remains.
async and await keywords removed, along with @frameSize. Settled: Zig gets no async/await keywords; asynchrony moves into the standard library Io interface. suspend/resume machinery may survive.

Concurrency is library-level: io.async(f,.{args}) yields a Future(T) with await(io) and cancel(io); io.concurrent() may return error.ConcurrencyUnavailable. Io.Threaded is complete; Io.Evented/Uring/Kqueue are experimental.

Io is now threaded through filesystem and network APIs: std.fs.Dir became std.Io.Dir, std.fs.File became std.Io.File, file.close() became file.close(io), File.read/write became readStreaming/writeStreaming, File.Mode became Permissions.

@Type is removed entirely. Use the split builtins @Int, @Struct, @Union, @Enum, @Fn, @Pointer, @Tuple, @EnumLiteral: @Type(.{.int=...}) becomes @Int(.unsigned, 10). std.meta.Int and std.meta.Tuple are deprecated alongside it.

Process and threading renames: std.process.Child.init became std.process.spawn, execv became process.replace; Thread.Mutex/Condition/ResetEvent became std.Io.Mutex/Condition/Event. Thread.Pool and Thread.Mutex.Recursive removed.

Deleted containers: std.BoundedArray, std.fifo.LinearFifo, std.RingBuffer, std.io.SeekableStream/BitReader/BitWriter (0.15.1); std.SegmentedList (0.16.0). std.DoublyLinkedList became intrusive — embed Node, recover parent via @fieldParentPtr.
replaces: std.BoundedArray, LinearFifo, RingBuffer, SegmentedList, generic DoublyLinkedList(T)

recipe: A type with a format method now requires the {f} specifier; bare {} on it is a compile error. New signature: format(self, w: *std.Io.Writer) std.Io.Writer.Error!void — no format string, no options.

std.fmt reshuffled again: Formatter became Alt, FormatOptions became Options, bufPrintZ became bufPrintSentinel, std.fmt.format became std.Io.Writer.print, and the {D} specifier became an Io.Duration format method.
callconv takes a tagged union, not an enum: write callconv(.c), not callconv(.C). Stack alignment is expressed as callconv(.withStackAlign(.c, 4)).

std.builtin.Type tags are lowercase: .Int became .int, .Struct became .@"struct", pointer size .One became .one. Reflection written against capitalized tags will not compile. @setCold became @branchHint(.cold).

GeneralPurposeAllocator was renamed DebugAllocator and rewritten. Top-level names deleted outright: std.rand became std.Random, std.TailQueue became std.DoublyLinkedList, std.ChildProcess became std.process.Child.
@fieldParentPtr lost its type argument — @fieldParentPtr("field", ptr), parent type inferred from result location. Also @errSetCast became @errorCast and @fabs became @abs (now integers too).

In build.zig, anonymous .{ .path = "src/main.zig" } LazyPaths are dead — use b.path(...). LazyPath.relative() deprecated. Separately, std.os was renamed std.posix; prefer cross-platform wrappers over it.
@cImport is deprecated; C translation moves into the build system via b.addTranslateC(). An official translate-c package is available as an explicit dependency for extra customization.

Canonical artifact: b.addExecutable(.{ .name, .root_module = b.createModule(.{ .root_source_file = b.path(...), .target, .optimize }) }). Deprecated implicit root_source_file fields on the artifact were removed in 0.15.1.
zig build --watch with -fincremental rebuilds only what changed; --debounce tunes filesystem settle time. Use --summary all to see which steps ran, their timing and memory.
build.zig.zon gained fingerprint (a permanent globally unique package id) and minimum_zig_version. Package hashes now embed name, version, fingerprint and unpacked size instead of bare hex.
replaces: hex-only package hashes, no fingerprint field

recipe: errdefer can capture the escaping error: errdefer |err| { ... }. Use it when cleanup or logging depends on which error propagated; plain defer still runs on success paths too.

unreachable is safety-checked illegal behavior: it panics in Debug and ReleaseSafe, but is exploitable undefined behavior in ReleaseFast/ReleaseSmall. std.debug.assert compiles to it — never assert on side-effecting expressions.
Error payloads (error.InvalidChar: usize) were proposed and closed as not planned. Errors stay plain tags — carry diagnostics in a caller-supplied out-parameter struct beside the error union.

Debug and ReleaseSafe write 0xaa over undefined memory, but that is an implementation aid, not a language semantic and not guaranteed observable. Never branch on it; reading undefined memory stays illegal behavior.
Choose overflow behavior explicitly: +% -% *% wrap two's-complement, +| -| *| saturate (@as(u8,255) +| 1 == 255). Plain + is a safety-checked trap, not silent wraparound.
*u8 and *align(1) u8 are now distinct types that merely coerce. Runtime indexing of a @Vector is a compile error, and array/vector in-memory coercion was removed — convert explicitly.
replaces: implicit array/vector in-memory coercion; vector[i] with runtime i

recipe: Zig has no default allocator. Take std.mem.Allocator as an explicit parameter, document ownership at the API boundary, and let callers pick arena, fixed-buffer or debug allocators.

std.testing.allocator makes the default test runner report leaks with allocation stack traces. Use std.testing.checkAllAllocationFailures to prove every allocation-failure path unwinds without leaking or double-freeing.
zig build test --fuzz runs the in-tree fuzzer and spawns a local HTTP server with live code-coverage visualization. std.testing.fuzz is the corresponding test-side entry point.
C23 makes bool, true, false, static_assert and thread_local keywords (still predefined macros for compatibility). <stdnoreturn.h> and the _Noreturn specifier are deprecated — use [[noreturn]].
Use nullptr and its type nullptr_t instead of NULL in C23. NULL's type is implementation-defined; nullptr is not.

C23 removes old-style non-prototype function declarations and definitions: int f() now means int f(void). C99 already removed implicit int and implicit function declarations. Never emit K&R parameter lists.
replaces: K&R parameter lists, implicit int, int f()

recipe: Never emit gets(): deprecated by C99 TC3, removed from the standard in C11. cppreference states outright "Never use gets()." Use fgets().

C99 gave you // comments, declarations at point of use, designated initializers, compound literals, flexible array members, snprintf, restrict, <stdint.h>, long long. Emitting C89 top-of-block declarations is decades stale.
C17/C18 added no features. It is C11 plus roughly 54 defect-report fixes (DR 400-491). There is no such thing as a C17 feature.

C23 adds binary literals 0b1010, digit separators 1'000'000, #embed, enums with fixed underlying type, auto type inference, typeof/typeof_unqual, constexpr objects, _BitInt(N), and the empty initializer = {}.

Use C23 standard attribute syntax [[nodiscard]], [[maybe_unused]], [[deprecated]], [[fallthrough]], [[noreturn]] rather than __attribute__((...)). Probe portability with __has_c_attribute in preprocessor conditionals.
static_assert is a C23 keyword and accepts a single argument with no message. _Static_assert is the C11 spelling, deprecated in C23.
C11 _Generic picks an expression by the controlling expression's type at compile time; unselected branches are never evaluated. Use it for type-generic macros instead of per-type name suffixes.
C23 <stddef.h> provides unreachable(); executing it is undefined behavior. Mark genuinely impossible branches so optimizers drop them and debug builds trap. It is not an error handler.
C23 adds memset_explicit() for explicit secure clearing of sensitive memory. A plain memset immediately before free is dead-store-eliminable.
C23 support is uneven: nullptr and constexpr need GCC 13 / Clang 16-19; #embed needs GCC 15 or Clang 19; typeof is partial in both. Contested whether to target C23 today.

VLAs are C99 but optional since C11 (__STDC_NO_VLA__); C23 keeps automatic-storage VLAs optional. Experts avoid them: unbounded stack growth, no failure path. Contested — some accept small bounded ones.

Annex K (memcpy_s, strcpy_s) is optional C11 and broadly rejected: WG14 N1967 reports no viable conforming implementations have emerged, and proposes removal or deprecation. Avoid _s functions outside MSVC.
source_name: WG14 N1967: Field Experience With Annex K

recipe: <threads.h> and <stdatomic.h> are C11 but optional — guard on __STDC_NO_THREADS__ / __STDC_NO_ATOMICS__. Contested: many projects still use pthreads or Win32 because C11 threads adoption lagged.
Use C99 flexible array members — empty [] as the last member, with at least one other named member — not the arr[1] struct hack. One malloc(sizeof(struct s) + n * sizeof(double)) covers both.
Publish an incomplete type in the header (struct string_mx; typedef struct string_mx string_mx;) and define it in the .c file. Callers cannot touch fields, so layout changes stay ABI-safe.
replaces: full struct definition in a public header

recipe: malloc(0) is implementation-defined — may return NULL, or a non-dereferenceable pointer you must still free. C23 makes realloc(p, 0) undefined behavior outright. Handle zero-size explicitly.

errno discipline: for in-band-error functions (strtol, strtod) set errno = 0 before the call, then inspect it. For out-of-band returns (ftell) check the return value first; never read errno unprompted.

Use a goto chain for multi-resource cleanup: one label per acquired resource, cascading releases in reverse order. CERT calls it the simplest and cleanest way — and says it does not license general goto.
replaces: duplicated cleanup at every error return

recipe: Avoid setjmp/longjmp. Undefined behavior if the setjmp function already returned, across threads, or after leaving a VLA scope; it also leaks VLAs on the way up. Return error codes.

Signed integer overflow is undefined behavior; implementations have considerable latitude. Test preconditions against INT_MAX/INT_MIN before adding, or use C23 ckd_add from <stdckdint.h>, which returns true on overflow.
replaces: post-hoc overflow checks like if (sum < a)

recipe: assert is disabled by NDEBUG as of the point <assert.h> is included, and the expression is then not evaluated at all — never put side effects inside. Contested whether asserts belong in shipped builds.

Accessing an object through an incompatible lvalue type is undefined. Taking an address, casting the pointer and dereferencing is undefined even through a union type, per GCC's own documented example.
-fstrict-aliasing is on by default at -O2, -O3 and -Os. Contested: some projects ship -fno-strict-aliasing rather than repair type punning, trading optimization for legacy-code survival.
i = ++i + 1;, a[i++] = i;, func(i++, i) are undefined — a side effect unsequenced relative to another side effect or value computation on the same scalar. Split into separate statements.
Shifting by a negative count, or by a count greater than or equal to the promoted left operand's width, is undefined. Validate against the type's precision before every variable shift.

Signed-to-unsigned conversion loses sign silently: (unsigned)INT_MIN becomes a huge positive value. Guard with if (si < 0) handle_error(); before converting — especially when an int length feeds a size_t parameter.

const-qualify immutable objects so the compiler warns on any write — CERT prefers this over swapping the variable for an enum constant or macro. Watch for const poisoning driving casts that strip const.

restrict promises that every access to an object modified through P happens through P within that block; otherwise undefined. Deleting every restrict must not change a conforming program's observable behavior.

OpenSSF production baseline: -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 -fstack-protector-strong -fstack-clash-protection -fcf-protection=full -fPIE -pie -Wl,-z,relro -Wl,-z,now -fstrict-flex-arrays=3 -ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero -fno-delete-null-pointer-checks.

Beyond -Wall -Wextra, OpenSSF recommends -Wformat=2 -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wimplicit-fallthrough -Wtrampolines for production. Blanket -Werror is development-only: it pins consumers to one toolchain vendor and version.

GCC -fanalyzer walks interprocedural paths for double-free, use-after-free, leaks, null deref, fd misuse, uninitialized values. GCC calls it neither sound nor complete — bug finder, not prover. C only.
Sanitizers do not all compose: -fsanitize=address cannot combine with thread or hwaddress, and thread cannot combine with leak. Run ASan+UBSan in one job and TSan in a separate job.
Build ASan at -O1 with -fno-omit-frame-pointer; add -fno-optimize-sibling-calls for perfect stack traces. Typical slowdown is 2x and it is not expected to produce false positives.
GCC's default C dialect is now gnu23 (gnu2x). Pin -std= explicitly in your build so a toolchain upgrade cannot silently change your language mode.

Valgrind Memcheck needs no recompilation and catches use of undefined values — a class ASan does not target. ASan headlines out-of-bounds, use-after-free, double-free, leaks. Different coverage; run both.

Fuzz entry point: int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *Data, size_t Size). Build with clang -g -O1 -fsanitize=fuzzer,address. Must be deterministic, fast, never exit. libFuzzer is now bugfix-only; authors moved to Centipede.
clang-tidy checks are globs under bugprone-, cert-, clang-analyzer-, misc-, performance-, readability-, modernize-. Select with -checks= and commit a .clang-tidy YAML so CI and editors agree.

For critical C, CBMC bounded-model-checks memory safety, array bounds, pointer safety, further undefined behavior and user assertions by unwinding loops into an equation for a SAT/SMT decision procedure.

Frama-C analyzes C through collaborative plugins over the ACSL specification language: plugins generate program annotations that other plugins then validate. Use it for requirement verification in high-assurance code.
